item.title: Search continues for 6 missing at sea as MSAF urges mariners to heed weather warnings
item.description: As the search continues for the 6 people who were travelling in a fibre glass boat between Namuka and Fulaga in the Lau Group, m ariners in maritme areas across Fiji are being urged to strictly follow active weather warnings. According to reports received by MSAF, the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre (JRCC) Fiji was notified yesterday that a half-cabin fibre glass boat powered by a 40-horsepower o
item.content:encoded:
As the search continues for the 6 people who were travelling in a fibre glass boat between Namuka and Fulaga in the Lau Group, m ariners in maritme areas across Fiji are being urged to strictly follow active weather warnings.

According to reports received by MSAF, the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre (JRCC) Fiji was notified yesterday that a half-cabin fibre glass boat powered by a 40-horsepower outboard engine had failed to arrive at its destination.

The vessel reportedly departed Namuka Island at around 10am yesterday bound for Fulaga Island.

Three fibre glass boats left Namuka that morning while two arrived safely in Fulaga, the third remains overdue with six people on board.

Following the report, JRCC Fiji, operating from the Vuvale Maritime Essential Services Centre (MESC), immediately activated search and rescue operations.

Navy Search and Rescue (SAR) mission coordinators have been working through the night, coordinating with government agencies, nearby vessels, and community contacts across the area.

Plans are underway to deploy both sea and air search assets today to widen the search effort.

Authorities are concerned that the missing vessel may not have been carrying essential life-saving equipment.

They say search operations are also being made more difficult by deteriorating weather conditions, including strong winds and rough to very rough seas.

They say despite these challenges, every effort remains focused on locating the vessel and bringing its occupants to safety.

M SAF is asking all mariners travelling between Namuka, Fulaga, and surrounding waters to keep a vigilant lookout for a white half-cabin fibreglass boat powered by a 40-horsepowe r outboard engine and its six occupants.

Anyone who sights the vessel or has information that could assist the search is urged to contact JRCC Fiji immediately on the toll-free number 1539 or report it to the nearest Police Station .

MSAF also reminds all mariners to take the nationwide Strong Wind Warning, issued on Thursday, 6 August 2026, seriously. The warning advises of southeasterly winds of 20 to 30 knots and rough to very rough sea conditions across affected areas.

In light of this incident, MSAF is reminding vessel owners and small-boat operators of their responsibilities to ensure safe operations at sea.

The search remains active, and further updates will be provided through official channels as confirmed information becomes available.

item.title: Nouzab Fareed to be sentenced on 27th August
item.description: Former Fijian Holdings Limited Chief Executive Officer Nouzab Fareed will be sentenced on 27th August for indecently assaulting a woman in his office as his lawyers seek a suspended sentence. Fareed 's lawyer Hemendra Nagin says they are also seeking a non-conviction for his client.
item.content:encoded:
Former Fijian Holdings Limited Chief Executive Officer Nouzab Fareed will be sentenced on 27th August for indecently assaulting a woman in his office as his lawyers seek a suspended sentence.

Fareed 's lawyer Hemendra Nagin says they are also seeking a non-conviction for his client.

Fareed appeared before Magistrate Josaia Waqaivolavola this morning.

State Prosecutor Sadaf Shameem told the Court that they are seeking a conviction and a custodial sentence.

The tariff for this is 12 months to 4 years.

item.title: One charged, three in custody after cocaine, meth and marijuana seizures
item.description: A joint task force raid on Nadi Back Road has resulted in the arrest of one man and the seizure of cocaine, methamphetamine and marijuana, while three more men remain in Police custody following two separate drug raids in Nadi and Natabua. Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations, Kasiano Vusonilawe says the raid on Nadi Back Road was carried out on Wednesday by the Joint Task Force comprising
item.content:encoded:
A joint task force raid on Nadi Back Road has resulted in the arrest of one man and the seizure of cocaine, methamphetamine and marijuana, while three more men remain in Police custody following two separate drug raids in Nadi and Natabua.

Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations, Kasiano Vusonilawe says the raid on Nadi Back Road was carried out on Wednesday by the Joint Task Force comprising the Fiji Police Force, the Republic of Fiji Military Forces and the Fiji Detector Dog Unit.

Vusonilawe says white substances seized during the operation tested positive for cocaine and methamphetamine, while dried leaves were confirmed to be marijuana.

He says the suspect has been charged with one count of unlawful possession of illicit drugs and will appear in the Nadi Magistrates' Court today.

The Assistant Commissioner says two more Joint Task Force raids were carried out yesterday at a car wash in Nadi and a home in Natabua.

He says the operations resulted in the seizure of white substances believed to be illicit drugs, and three men were arrested.

Vusonilawe says the three men remain in Police custody while the seized substances have been sent for analysis.

Meanwhile, the suspect arrested during another Joint Task Force raid in Lautoka on Tuesday, following the seizure of methamphetamine, has been charged and appeared in the Lautoka Magistrates' Court yesterday.

Police are urging people to report drug-related activities by calling the Crime Stoppers line on 1681.

item.title: Supreme Court to decide whether Rahman faces retrial or acquittal in 39.5kg cocaine case
item.description: The Supreme Court will decide at a later date whether Fiji-Canadian national Joshua Aziz Rahman should face a new trial or be acquitted over the 39.5 kilograms of cocaine worth $31 million found at a Caubati home in 2019. Rahman was sentenced to 23 years' imprisonment in October 2021, with a non-parole period of 14 years, after his conviction, but was released in March this year after the Court of
item.content:encoded:
The Supreme Court will decide at a later date whether Fiji-Canadian national Joshua Aziz Rahman should face a new trial or be acquitted over the 39.5 kilograms of cocaine worth $31 million found at a Caubati home in 2019.

Rahman was sentenced to 23 years' imprisonment in October 2021, with a non-parole period of 14 years, after his conviction, but was released in March this year after the Court of Appeal quashed his conviction and ordered a retrial.

He then appealed the Court of Appeal's decision ordering a retrial through his counsel, Devnesh Sharma.

During the hearing, Sharma argued that the prosecution's case has serious evidential weaknesses, saying there is no proof Rahman knew the cocaine was in the house, no forensic evidence linking him to the drugs or the bedroom where they were found, no evidence he handled the drugs, and no evidence he had control over them.

He says the prosecution has also failed to rule out the possibility that Rahman 's father, Tallat Rahman, was solely responsible for the drugs.

He further submits that Rahman has spent more than seven years in custody, memories have faded, a key witness has died, and police investigations were inadequate.

Sharma also argues that investigators failed to carry out fingerprint or DNA testing, examine Rahman 's electronic devices, investigate imports linked to the property, obtain CCTV footage, or gather evidence that could establish Rahman 's knowledge or control of the drugs.

He says a retrial would unfairly give the prosecution a second chance to repair deficiencies in its original case, adding that the Supreme Court should acquit him, and not order a new trial.

In their submission, Acting Director of Public Prosecutions Nancy Tikoisuva argued that the Court of Appeal should not have ordered a retrial, but also says the appeal by Rahman should have been dismissed entirely because there was no substantial miscarriage of justice.

She submits that the Court of Appeal failed to assess all the evidence before deciding to quash the conviction and order a retrial, and did not properly apply the legal test in the Court of Appeal Act.

Tikoisuva argued there was strong direct and circumstantial evidence against the Rahman and that, even if there were legal errors, a properly directed court would still have convicted him.

She says that the Court of Appeal did not properly consider the interests of justice before ordering a retrial and that both parties should have been allowed to address that issue.

The Acting DPP also objected to Rahman's attempt to rely on renewed grounds of appeal and new evidence, arguing these should have been raised separately and should not affect the retrial decision.

They ask the Supreme Court to dismiss the Rahman's appeal, maintaining that the correct outcome was to dismiss the original appeal rather than order a retrial.

item.title: 4 Police officers charged with assault and theft
item.description: Four police officers will appear before the Suva Magistrates Court today in relation to an alleged assault that occurred in August 2024. Police say the four officers questioned a victim after he allegedly caused a disturbance at a barbecue stall during the morning of 25th August 2024 and it is further alleged that the victim was assaulted following the questioning.
item.content:encoded:
Four police officers will appear before the Suva Magistrates Court today in relation to an alleged assault that occurred in August 2024.

Police say the four officers questioned a victim after he allegedly caused a disturbance at a barbecue stall during the morning of 25th August 2024 and it is further alleged that the victim was assaulted following the questioning.

Police say one of the officers is also alleged to have stolen the victim's personal belongings after the assault.

Following the completion of investigations, the case file was referred to the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions, which advised that formal charges be laid.

Police says the four officers have been jointly charged with one count of acts intended to cause grievous harm.

One officer also faces an additional charge of theft.

All four officers have been suspended pending the outcome of the court proceedings.

The Fiji Police Force maintains a zero-tolerance approach to any abuse of legal authority by its officers.

Police say all complaints and official reports involving allegations of police misconduct are thoroughly investigated by the Internal Affairs Division.

Where evidence indicates the commission of a criminal offence, the matter is referred to the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) for investigation.

Police says upon completion of a criminal investigation, case files are submitted to the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions for independent legal advice, ensuring transparency, accountability, and independent oversight throughout the investigative process.

item.title: Three men in custody over alleged break-in at Valelevu property
item.description: Three men have been remanded in custody after they were allegedly caught breaking into a property in Valelevu that is currently under a High Court restraining order linked to an unexplained wealth case. Police say the three men, aged 35, 36 and 46, were arrested by officers from the Serious Organised Crime and Intelligence Department and the Criminal Investigations Department.
item.content:encoded:
Three men have been remanded in custody after they were allegedly caught breaking into a property in Valelevu that is currently under a High Court restraining order linked to an unexplained wealth case.

Police say the three men, aged 35, 36 and 46, were arrested by officers from the Serious Organised Crime and Intelligence Department and the Criminal Investigations Department.

Police say the accused have been jointly charged with one count each of damaging property, unlawful possession of illicit drugs, and possession of property suspected to be the proceeds of crime.

They first appeared in the Nasinu Magistrates' Court on Monday, where they were remanded in custody and ordered to reappear the following day for the determination of their bail application.

The three men are scheduled to appear in court again today for the hearing of their bail application.

item.title: Seaqaqa cane farmer questions sugar shortage and delayed land lease
item.description: A Seaqaqa cane farmer is demanding answers on when she will receive the lease to her land after paying the lease premium, saying she needs it to start planting cane. Speaking during the Special Committee on the Sugar Industry's public consultation, Sheila Wati says she wants to plant cane but is helpless without the lease.
item.content:encoded:
A Seaqaqa cane farmer is demanding answers on when she will receive the lease to her land after paying the lease premium, saying she needs it to start planting cane.

Speaking during the Special Committee on the Sugar Industry's public consultation, Sheila Wati says she wants to plant cane but is helpless without the lease.

Wati also questioned why there is a shortage of sugar in Seaqaqa.

The cane farmer says it is concerning that cane farmers are having to go from shop to shop just to buy a kilogram of sugar.

Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka, who is also the Chair of the Special Committee, requested the Fiji Sugar Corporation Chief Executive Officer to take her details so that a response could be provided later.

Meanwhile, Minister for Agriculture and Sugar Tomasi Tunabuna confirmed to fijivillage News that there is currently no shortage of raw sugar, with the Fiji Sugar Corporation confirming that supermarkets have stock available as the sugar mills increase production to improve local supply.

Further questions have been sent to FSC and the Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission.

Questions have also been sent to the iTaukei Land Trust Board regarding the lease issue.
